about: Manawydan, Pryderi, Rhiannon and Cigfa come back from England to empty Dyfed and live by hunting at Arberth. One morning the dogs flush a shining white boar from a thicket and follow it into a great new fort where no fort ever stood; Pryderi, against Manawydan's counsel, goes in after them, takes hold of a bowl above a marble slab, with chains rising into the air, and sticks fast, speechless. Rhiannon, rebuking Manawydan, goes to find him, sticks fast in her turn, and with a noise and a shower of mist the fort vanishes and they with it. Manawydan swears to Cigfa that he will keep faith with her, takes her into England, where he works again as a shoemaker until the shoemakers plot to kill him, and brings her back to Arberth with a load of wheat. He sows three crofts; two are stripped of their ears the night before reaping, and watching the third he sees a numberless host of mice carry off the corn, and catches one that is too heavy to run.

sentences.t: Byhyt bynnac y buant ar y fford, wynt a doethant y Dyuet, ac Arberth a gyrchyssant.
sentences.l: However-long they-were on the road, they it-was-that came to Dyfed, and Arberth it-was-that they-made-for.
sentences.i: However long they were on the road, they came to Dyfed, and made for Arberth.
sentences.n: The journey formula of the last part, which ends with the four making for Dyfed. Byhyt bynnac 'whatever length': Byhyt is pa hyt 'what length' written as one word and spelt with b and y (008 has A pha hyt bynnac); bynnac '-ever'. y buant 'they were', 3 pl. preterite of bot. fford is ffordd 'road', here with ff (008 ford). wynt a doethant 'they came' and Arberth a gyrchyssant 'Arberth they made for': the abnormal sentence twice, the second time with the object put first; gyrchyssant ← kyrchyssant, 3 pl. preterite of kyrchu, softened after a.

sentences.t: A llad tan a wnaethant, a dechreu ymborth, a hela, a threulaw mis yuelly, a chynnull eu cwn attunt, a hela, a bot yuelly yno ulwydyn.
sentences.l: And kindling fire they-did, and beginning to-feed-themselves, and hunting, and spending a month so, and gathering their dogs to-them, and hunting, and being so there a-year.
sentences.i: They kindled a fire and began to keep themselves, hunting; they spent a month so, and gathered their dogs about them, and hunted, and lived there in that way for a year.
sentences.n: A llad tan a wnaethant 'striking fire they did': a verbal noun, then a and a form of gwneuthur 'do' — one of the two great narrative patterns, meaning simply 'they kindled a fire' (llad 'strike, kill'). The verbal nouns that follow (dechreu, hela, treulaw, kynnull, bot) carry on the narrative with no finite verb. ymborth 'feed oneself, get a living'. a threulaw ← treulaw 'spend', a chynnull ← kynnull 'gather': the spirant mutation after a 'and'. attunt 'to them', at conjugated, 3 pl. ulwydyn ← blwydyn 'year', softened as an expression of time; u writes /v/.

sentences.t: A boregueith, kyuodi Pryderi a Manawydan y hela; a chyweiraw eu cwn, a mynet odieithyr y llys.
sentences.l: And one-morning, rising Pryderi and Manawydan to hunt; and making-ready their dogs, and going outside the court.
sentences.i: And one morning Pryderi and Manawydan rose to go hunting; they made ready their dogs, and went out of the court.
sentences.n: boregueith 'one morning' (bore + gweith 'time'), like treigylgweith in the First Branch. kyuodi Pryderi a Manawydan 'rising Pryderi and Manawydan': the verbal noun with its subjects straight after it, standing for 'they rose'. y hela 'to hunt': y 'to' with the verbal noun. a chyweiraw ← kyweiraw 'prepare, make ready', spirant after a. odieithyr 'outside'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth rei o'e cwn, kerdet o'e wlaen, a mynet y berth uechan oed gyr eu llaw.
sentences.l: That-is what did some of their dogs: going before-them, and going to a bush little that-was near their hand.
sentences.i: Some of their dogs ran on ahead of them, and went to a little thicket close at hand.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth rei o'e cwn, kerdet 'that is what some of their dogs did: going': sef ('that is') announces the deed, which follows as a verbal noun. o'e 'of their' (o + 'e, the possessive). o'e wlaen 'in front of them': the phrase o ulaen 'in front of' (blaen 'front', with the fixed soft mutation b > f), with 'their' put inside it. The White Book writes the softened b with w (Evans prints the 6-shaped w, certain on the image), where the second witness and the Red Book have blaen; kept as written, compare Vynt for wynt in 008. y berth uechan 'to a little bush': perth softened after y 'to'; uechan ← bechan, the feminine of bychan 'small', softened after the feminine noun. oed gyr eu llaw 'that was near their hand': the relative particle is not written before oed; gyr 'beside, near'.

sentences.t: Ac y gyt ac yd aant y'r berth, kilyaw y gyflym, a cheginwrych mawr aruthyr ganthunt, ac ymchwelut at y guyr.
sentences.l: And as-soon-as they-go to-the bush, retreating quickly, and bristles great terrible with-them, and turning-back to the men.
sentences.i: And as soon as they reached the thicket they fell back fast, their hackles up, huge and dreadful, and turned back to the men.
sentences.n: Ac y gyt ac 'and together with' = as soon as. yd aant 'they go': aant, 3 pl. present of mynet, the vivid present in past narrative; yd is the particle before a vowel. y'r 'to the'. kilyaw 'retreat, fall back'. y gyflym 'quickly' ← kyflym, softened after y in an adverb. keginwrych (here a cheginwrych, spirant after a) is the bristling of the back, hackles raised (gwrych 'bristles'); mawr aruthyr 'great, terrible'. ganthunt 'with them', gan conjugated, 3 pl. ymchwelut 'turn back'. y guyr 'the men' (gwyr, spelt gu-).

sentences.t: “Nessawn,” heb y Pryderi, “parth a'r berth, y edrych beth yssyd yndi.”
sentences.l: “Let-us-draw-near,” said Pryderi, “towards the bush, to see what is in-it.”
sentences.i: “Let us go closer to the thicket,” said Pryderi, “and see what is in it.”
sentences.n: Nessawn 'let us draw near', 1 pl. imperative of nessau. heb y Pryderi 'said Pryderi': before a named speaker heb takes y. parth a'r 'towards the'. beth ← peth 'what', softened. yssyd 'which is', the relative form of bot. yndi 'in it', yn conjugated, 3 sg. feminine, for perth.

sentences.t: Nessau parth a'r berth.
sentences.l: Drawing-near towards the bush.
sentences.i: They drew near the thicket.
sentences.n: The verbal noun nessau alone stands for the whole sentence 'they drew near'.

sentences.t: Pan nessaant, llyma uaed coed claerwynn yn kyuodi o'r berth; sef a oruc y cwn, o hyder y guyr, ruthraw idaw.
sentences.l: When they-draw-near, behold a boar of-wood shining-white rising from the bush; that-is what did the dogs, from confidence of the men, rushing at-it.
sentences.i: When they came near, there was a shining white wild boar rising out of the thicket; and the dogs, emboldened by the men, rushed at it.
sentences.n: Pan nessaant 'when they draw near', present again. llyma 'behold, here is' throws the scene before the reader's eyes, and softens what follows: uaed ← baed 'boar'. baed coed 'boar of the wood', a wild boar. claerwynn 'shining white', a compound of claer 'bright' and gwynn 'white'. sef a oruc y cwn … ruthraw idaw 'that is what the dogs did: rushing at it': oruc is the preterite of the defective verb that serves gwneuthur. o hyder y guyr 'out of the confidence of the men', heartened by them. ruthraw is rhuthraw 'rush', r writing rh. idaw 'to it', y conjugated, 3 sg.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ynteu, adaw y berth, a chilyaw dalym y wrth y guyr.
sentences.l: That-is what did he-for-his-part: leaving the bush, and retreating a-little-way from the men.
sentences.i: And it left the thicket, and drew back a little way from the men.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth ynteu, adaw 'that is what it did: leaving'. ynteu 'he for his part', the boar. a chilyaw ← kilyaw 'retreat'. dalym ← talym 'a space, a while', softened as an adverb: 'a little way'. y wrth 'away from'.

sentences.t: Ac yny uei agos y guyr idaw, kyuarth a rodei y'r cwn, heb gilyaw yrdhunt.
sentences.l: And until would-be near the men to-it, a-baying it-was-that it-would-give to-the dogs, without retreating from-them.
sentences.i: Until the men came close to it, it would stand at bay to the dogs, without giving ground before them.
sentences.n: yny 'until'; uei ← bei, imperfect subjunctive of bot, softened after yny. agos 'near'. kyuarth a rodei 'a baying it would give': kyuarth is the baying of hounds round a beast, and a beast that gives kyuarth stands at bay; rodei is the imperfect of rodi 'give', here of repeated action. heb gilyaw ← kilyaw, softened after heb. yrdhunt is so written (dh, an unusual spelling for the /ð/ sound) and is kept; it is a conjugated preposition, 3 pl., 'from them' or 'before them', perhaps a form of rac (racdunt), but the form is uncertain.

sentences.t: A phan ynghei y guyr, y kilyei eilweith, ac y torrei gyuarth.
sentences.l: And when would-close-in the men, it-would-retreat again, and it-would-break bay.
sentences.i: And when the men closed in, it would fall back again, and stand at bay once more.
sentences.n: A phan ← pan 'when', spirant after a. ynghei 'would draw close': the imperfect of a verb related to yng 'narrow, close'; the meaning 'close in, come near' is from the context. y kilyei … y torrei 'it would retreat … it would break', imperfects of kilyaw and torri, each with the particle y. torri kyuarth 'break bay' — gyuarth softened as the object — seems to mean that the boar turned and made a stand again; the exact sense of the phrase is not certain. eilweith 'a second time, again'.

sentences.t: Ac yn ol y baed y kerdassant, yny welynt gaer uawr aruchel, a gueith newyd arnei, yn lle ny welsynt na maen na gueith eiryoet; a'r baed yn kyrchu yr gaer yn uuan, a'r cwn yn y ol.
sentences.l: And after the boar it-was-that they-walked, until they-saw a-fort great very-high, and work new on-it, in a place they-had-not-seen either stone or work ever; and the boar making-for the fort swiftly, and the dogs after it.
sentences.i: And they followed the boar until they saw a great, towering fort, newly built, in a place where they had never seen stone or building; and the boar was making swiftly for the fort, and the dogs after it.
sentences.n: yn ol y baed y kerdassant 'after the boar they walked': the phrase put first, then the particle y. kerdassant 3 pl. preterite of kerdet. yny welynt 'until they saw' (gwelynt, imperfect, softened after yny). gaer ← kaer 'fort', softened as the object; uawr ← mawr after the feminine noun. aruchel 'very high' (ar- + uchel). gueith newyd arnei 'new work on it', fresh stonework. ny welsynt 'they had not seen', 3 pl. pluperfect. na … na 'either … or' after the negative. eiryoet 'ever'. yr gaer: yr is read as the article ('the fort'), as the second witness takes it; uuan ← buan 'swift'. yn y ol 'after it', literally 'in its track'.

sentences.t: A guedy mynet y baed a'r cwn y'r gaer, ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer yn y lle ny welsynt eiryoet weith kyn no hynny, ac o ben yr orssed edrych a wnaethant, ac ymwarandaw a'r cwn.
sentences.l: And after going the boar and the dogs into-the fort, marvelling they-did to-see the fort in the place they-had-not-seen ever building before that, and from top of-the mound looking they-did, and listening for the dogs.
sentences.i: And when the boar and the dogs had gone into the fort, they marvelled to see the fort in that place, where they had never seen any building before; and from the top of the mound they watched, and listened for the dogs.
sentences.n: guedy mynet y baed a'r cwn 'after going the boar and the dogs': guedy 'after' with the verbal noun, its subjects after it. ryuedu a wnaethant 'marvelling they did'. welet ← gwelet, softened after the verb. weith ← gweith 'work, building', softened as the object of welsynt (it could also be gweith 'time', 'ever a time', but the building is the point). kyn no hynny 'before that'. o ben ← penn, softened after o. yr orssed ← gorssed 'mound', softened after the feminine article: presumably the Mound of Arberth. ymwarandaw a 'listen to, listen for'.

sentences.t: Pa hyt bynnac y bydynt yuelly, ny chlywynt un o'r cwn na dim y wrthunt.
sentences.l: However-long they-were thus, they-did-not-hear one of-the dogs nor anything from-them.
sentences.i: However long they stayed so, they heard not one of the dogs, nor any news of them.
sentences.n: Pa hyt bynnac 'however long', here written as three words. y bydynt 'they were', the habitual past of bot. ny chlywynt 'they did not hear': klywynt with the spirant after ny. y wrthunt 'from them, about them', y wrth conjugated, 3 pl.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Pryderi, “mi a af y'r gaer, y geissaw chwedleu y wrth y cwn.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Pryderi, “I it-is-that will-go into-the fort, to seek tidings about the dogs.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Pryderi, “I will go into the fort and seek news of the dogs.”
sentences.n: mi a af 'I will go': af, 1 sg. present of mynet, the abnormal sentence with a pronoun. y geissaw ← keissaw 'seek', softened after y 'to'. chwedleu 'tidings, news', plural of chwedyl.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb ynteu, “nyt da dy gynghor uynet y'r gaer honn yma eiryoet. Ac o gwney uyg hynghor i, nyt ey idi. A'r neb a dodes hut ar y wlat, a beris bot y gaer yma.”
sentences.l: “Surely,” said he-for-his-part, “not good your counsel, to-go into-the fort this here ever. And if you-do my counsel, you-will-not-go into-it. And the one who put enchantment on the land, it-was-that caused the fort to-be here.”
sentences.i: “Surely,” he said, “it is not good counsel of yours, to go into this fort that was never here before. And if you take my counsel, you will not go into it. Whoever laid the enchantment on the land has caused the fort to be here.”
sentences.n: Dioer 'surely, indeed' (as in 008). heb ynteu 'said he for his part' (house): Manawydan. dy gynghor ← kynghor, softened after dy 'your'; uynet ← mynet, softened. The clause y'r gaer honn yma eiryoet 'into this fort here ever' has no verb for eiryoet: the White Book is elliptic here (no gap on the page), meaning 'this fort that never was here'; the Red Book reads y'r gaer honn nys gweleist eiryoet 'this fort, which you never saw', and the second witness supplies words of its own. Nothing is supplied. o gwney 'if you do': o 'if' causes no mutation; gwney, 2 sg. present of gwneuthur. uyg hynghor 'my counsel': uy 'my' causes nasal mutation, kynghor > nghynghor, and the White Book writes it with g on the possessive and h on the noun (uyg hynghor; compare uyg kwn below). nyt ey 'you will not go', ey 2 sg. present of mynet; idi 'into it', y conjugated, 3 sg. feminine. A'r neb a dodes 'and the one who put': dodes, 3 sg. preterite of dodi. hut 'enchantment, spell'. a beris ← peris, 3 sg. preterite of peri 'cause', softened after a.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb y Pryderi, “ny madeuaf i uyg kwn.”
sentences.l: “Surely,” said Pryderi, “I-will-not-give-up I my dogs.”
sentences.i: “Surely,” said Pryderi, “I will not abandon my dogs.”
sentences.n: ny madeuaf 'I will not forsake': madeu (maddau) is 'forgive' and also 'give up, let go'. After ny one would expect the softened uadeuaf; the m is written unmutated. uyg kwn 'my dogs': uy with the nasal mutation written g + k (= fy nghwn); kwn is cwn spelt with k.

sentences.t: Pa gynghor bynnac a gaffei ef y gan Uanawydan, y gaer a gyrchwys ef.
sentences.l: Whatever counsel he-would-get from Manawydan, the fort it-was-that he-made-for.
sentences.i: Whatever counsel he had from Manawydan, he made for the fort.
sentences.n: Pa gynghor bynnac 'whatever counsel' ← kynghor, softened after pa. a gaffei ← kaffei, imperfect of caffael 'get', softened after a. y gan 'from'. Uanawydan ← Manawydan, softened after gan. y gaer a gyrchwys 'the fort he made for': the object first; kyrchwys, 3 sg. preterite in -wys of kyrchu, softened after a.

sentences.t: Pan doeth y'r gaer, na dyn, na mil, na'r baed, na'r cwn, na thy, nac anhed, ny welei yn y gaer.
sentences.l: When he-came into-the fort, neither man, nor beast, nor the boar, nor the dogs, nor house, nor dwelling, did-he-not-see in the fort.
sentences.i: When he came into the fort, he saw neither man nor beast, nor the boar, nor the dogs, nor house nor dwelling in it.
sentences.n: doeth 'came', 3 sg. preterite of dyuot. The list of things not seen stands first, each with na (nac before a vowel), and the verb comes last with its own negative: ny welei 'he did not see', gwelei, imperfect, softened after ny. mil 'animal, beast'. na thy ← ty 'house', spirant after na. anhed 'dwelling'.

sentences.t: Ef a welei, ual am gymherued llawr y gaer, fynnawn a gueith o uaen marmor yn y chylch.
sentences.l: He it-was-that saw, as-it-were about middle of-the floor of the fort, a-well and work of stone marble in its circle.
sentences.i: He saw, about the middle of the floor of the fort, a well, with a stonework of marble round it.
sentences.n: Ef a welei 'he saw'. ual 'as, as it were', softening the precision of what follows. am gymherued ← kymherued 'middle', softened after am 'about'. fynnawn is ffynnawn 'spring, well', f for ff. gueith 'work', here stonework. o uaen ← maen 'stone', softened after o; maen marmor 'marble stone'. yn y chylch 'in its circle' = round it: kylch with the spirant after y 'its' (feminine, for ffynnawn).

sentences.t: Ac ar lann y fynnawn, cawg uch benn llech o uaen marmor, a chadwyneu yn kyrchu yr awyr, a diben ny welei arnunt.
sentences.l: And on the bank of the well, a-bowl above a-slab of stone marble, and chains reaching-to the air, and end he-did-not-see on-them.
sentences.i: And at the edge of the well there was a bowl, above a slab of marble, and chains going up into the air, and he could see no end to them.
sentences.n: There is no verb: a list of what was there. ar lann ← glann 'bank, edge', softened after ar. cawg 'bowl' (spelt cawc in the next sentence). uch benn 'above' ← penn, softened after uch. llech 'slab'. a chadwyneu ← kadwyneu 'chains', spirant after a. Evans prints a blank after chadwyneu at the end of the line, a gap in the manuscript; nothing is supplied, and the sentence stands as it is. The White Book never says here that the bowl is gold, although the next sentence speaks of yr eur 'the gold'; the Red Book has kawc eur 'a gold bowl', and the second witness supplies a clause about four chains. yn kyrchu yr awyr 'making for the air', rising into it. diben 'end', put before ny welei 'he did not see'. arnunt 'on them', ar conjugated, 3 pl.

sentences.t: Gorawenu a wnaeth ynteu wrth decket yr eur, a dahet gueith y cawc; a dyuot a wnaeth yn yd oed y cawc, ac ymauael ac ef.
sentences.l: Rejoicing he-did for-his-part at fairness of-the gold, and goodness of-the work of the bowl; and coming he-did to where was the bowl, and taking-hold of it.
sentences.i: He was delighted by the fairness of the gold and the fineness of the bowl's workmanship; and he went to where the bowl was, and took hold of it.
sentences.n: Gorawenu a wnaeth 'rejoicing he did': gorawenu 'rejoice, be elated'. wrth decket 'at (how) fair': tecket, the equative of tec, used as a noun 'fairness', softened after wrth. yr eur 'the gold' (aur): see the note above, the bowl has not been called gold. dahet is the equative of da 'good', with h, used the same way: 'how good the work of the bowl'. yn yd oed 'where it was'. ymauael ac 'take hold of', with ac, the preposition a before a vowel.

sentences.t: Ac y gyt ac yd ymeueil a'r cawc, glynu y dwylaw wrth y cawc, a'y draet wrth y llech yd oed yn seuyll arnei, a dwyn y lywenyd y gantaw, hyt na allei dywedut un geir.
sentences.l: And as-soon-as he-takes-hold of-the bowl, sticking his two-hands to the bowl, and his feet to the slab that he-was standing on-it, and taking his joy from-him, so-that he-could-not say one word.
sentences.i: And as soon as he took hold of the bowl, his hands stuck to the bowl, and his feet to the slab on which he was standing, and his joy was taken from him, so that he could not say a single word.
sentences.n: yd ymeueil 'he takes hold', 3 sg. present of ymauael (the a of the stem becomes e): the vivid present again. glynu 'stick'. y dwylaw 'his two hands', the dual of llaw. a'y draet 'and his feet': a + 'y 'his', which softens traet. yd oed yn seuyll arnei 'that he was standing on it': the relative clause has yd and closes with arnei 'on it' (ar, 3 sg. feminine, for llech). a dwyn y lywenyd y gantaw 'and taking his joy from him': llywenyd 'joy', softened after y 'his'; so the White Book (and the Red Book y lewenyd), plain on the image. The second witness prints lyueryd, 'his speech', a modern editor's emendation, not the manuscript's reading. y gantaw 'from him'. hyt na allei 'so that he could not': gallei softened after na. un geir ← geir 'word', softened after un.

sentences.t: A seuyll a wnaeth yuelly.
sentences.l: And standing he-did thus.
sentences.i: And so he stood.
sentences.n: seuyll 'stand', with a wnaeth: 'he stood'. yuelly 'thus' (felly).

sentences.t: A'e aros ynteu a wnaeth Manawydan hyt parth a diwed y dyd.
sentences.l: And his-waiting for-his-part did Manawydan until towards end of the day.
sentences.i: And Manawydan, for his part, waited for him until near the end of the day.
sentences.n: A'e aros … a wnaeth Manawydan 'and his waiting did Manawydan': 'e 'his' before the verbal noun aros 'wait' marks its object, 'waiting for him'; the subject comes after a wnaeth. ynteu 'he for his part'. hyt parth a diwed 'till towards the end'.

sentences.t: A phrynhawn byrr, guedy bot yn diheu gantaw ef na chaei chwedleu y wrth Pryderi nac y wrth y cwn, dyuot a oruc parth a'r llys.
sentences.l: And afternoon short, after being certain with-him he that he-would-not-get tidings from Pryderi nor from the dogs, coming he-did towards the court.
sentences.i: And late in the afternoon, when he was sure he would have no news of Pryderi or of the dogs, he came back towards the court.
sentences.n: A phrynhawn byrr 'and a short afternoon': prynhawn with the spirant after a; the afternoon grown short, that is, late. guedy bot yn diheu gantaw ef 'after it being certain with him' = when he was sure. na chaei 'that he would not get': kaei, imperfect of caffael, with the spirant after na. dyuot a oruc 'coming he did'.

sentences.t: Pan daw y mywn, sef a wnaeth Riannon, edrych arnaw.
sentences.l: When he-comes inside, that-is what did Rhiannon: looking at-him.
sentences.i: When he came in, Rhiannon looked at him.
sentences.n: Pan daw 'when he comes': daw, 3 sg. present of dyuot. y mywn 'inside'. sef a wnaeth Riannon, edrych 'that is what Rhiannon did: looking'. arnaw 'at him', ar conjugated, 3 sg.

sentences.t: “Mae,” heb hi, “dy gedymdeith di, a'th cwn?”
sentences.l: “Where-is,” said she, “your companion you, and your dogs?”
sentences.i: “Where,” she said, “is your companion, and your dogs?”
sentences.n: Mae 'where is', the interrogative, as in 008. heb hi 'said she'. dy gedymdeith ← kedymdeith 'companion', softened after dy; di 'you' repeats the possessive. a'th cwn 'and your dogs': a + 'th 'your', which usually softens; here cwn is written unsoftened.

sentences.t: “Llyma,” heb ynteu, “uyg kyfranc,” a'e datcanu oll.
sentences.l: “Here-is,” said he-for-his-part, “my adventure,” and its recounting all.
sentences.i: “Here,” he said, “is what befell me,” and he told it all.
sentences.n: Llyma 'here is'. uyg kyfranc 'my adventure': kyfranc 'encounter, adventure, story', with the nasal after uy written as in uyg kwn. a'e datcanu 'and its declaring': 'e is the object 'it', datcanu 'declare, relate'; the verbal noun stands for 'and he told'. oll 'all'.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb y Riannon, “ys drwc a gedymdeith uuosti, ac ys da a gedymdeith a golleisti.”
sentences.l: “Surely,” said Rhiannon, “it-is bad a companion you-were, and it-is good a companion that you-lost.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” said Rhiannon, “a poor companion you have been, and a good companion you have lost.”
sentences.n: ys 'it is', the old form of the copula, with the predicate put first: ys drwc 'bad it is'. drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion': the adjective first, joined to the noun by a, which softens kedymdeith; the construction is old and a is not the conjunction (that would give chedymdeith). uuosti 'you were': buost, 2 sg. preterite of bot, softened, with ti fused on. a golleisti 'that you lost': colleist, softened after the relative a, with ti.

sentences.t: A chan y geir hwnnw mynet allan, ac y traws y managassei ef uot y gwr a'r gaer, kyrchu a wnaeth hitheu.
sentences.l: And with the word that going out, and to the quarter that he-had-shown being the man and the fort, making-for she-did for-her-part.
sentences.i: And with that word she went out, and made for the quarter where he had told her the man and the fort were.
sentences.n: A chan ← can 'with', spirant after a. mynet allan 'going out'. y traws 'the direction, the quarter' (traws 'across, crosswise'). y managassei ef 'that he had shown': managassei, pluperfect of managu 'show, tell', the ending -assei. uot ← bot, softened after the verb: 'that the man and the fort were'. kyrchu a wnaeth hitheu 'making for she did': hitheu 'she for her part'.

sentences.t: Porth y gaer a welas yn agoret; ny bu argel arnei.
sentences.l: The gate of the fort she-saw open; there-was-not concealment on-it.
sentences.i: She found the gate of the fort open; nothing about it was hidden.
sentences.n: Porth y gaer a welas 'the gate of the fort she saw': the object first; gwelas, 3 sg. preterite, softened after a. yn agoret 'open', predicative yn. ny bu 'there was not', preterite of bot. argel 'hiding, concealment': the gate was not shut or screened. arnei 'on it', ar, 3 sg. feminine.

sentences.t: Ac y mywn y doeth, ac y gyt ac y doeth, arganuot Pryderi yn ymauael a'r cawc, a dyuot attaw.
sentences.l: And inside it-was-that she-came, and as-soon-as she-came, catching-sight-of Pryderi taking-hold of-the bowl, and coming to-him.
sentences.i: And she came in, and as soon as she came in she caught sight of Pryderi with his hold on the bowl, and went to him.
sentences.n: y mywn y doeth 'inside she came': the adverb first, then the particle y. y gyt ac 'as soon as'. arganuot 'catch sight of'. yn ymauael a'r cawc 'gripping the bowl'. attaw 'to him', at conjugated, 3 sg.

sentences.t: “Och, uy Arglwyd,” heb hi, “beth a wney di yma?”
sentences.l: “Oh, my Lord,” said she, “what is-it-that you-do you here?”
sentences.i: “Ah, my lord,” she said, “what are you doing here?”
sentences.n: Och 'oh, ah', a cry of distress. uy Arglwyd 'my lord'. beth ← peth 'what', softened. a wney di 'that you do': gwney, 2 sg. present of gwneuthur, softened after a; di is ti softened.

sentences.t: Ac ymauael a'r cawc y gyt ac ef.
sentences.l: And taking-hold of-the bowl together with him.
sentences.i: And she took hold of the bowl with him.
sentences.n: ymauael a'r cawc: the verbal noun again carries the narrative. y gyt ac ef 'together with him'.

sentences.t: Ac y gyt ac yd ymeueil, glynu y dwylaw hitheu wrth y cawc, a'y deutroet wrth y llech, hyt na allei hitheu dywedut un geir.
sentences.l: And as-soon-as she-takes-hold, sticking her two-hands she-for-her-part to the bowl, and her two-feet to the slab, so-that she-could-not she-for-her-part say one word.
sentences.i: And as soon as she took hold, her own hands stuck to the bowl, and her two feet to the slab, so that she too could not say a word.
sentences.n: The words of Pryderi's sticking, said again of Rhiannon. y dwylaw hitheu 'her two hands': y here is 'her', which gives the spirant mutation, but d does not show it; hitheu 'she for her part' after the noun makes 'her' plain. a'y deutroet 'and her two feet': deu 'two' + troet 'foot', a dual compound.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny, gyt ac y bu nos, llyma dwryf arnunt, a chawat o nywl, a chan hynny difflannu y gaer, ac e ymdeith ac wynteu.
sentences.l: And upon that, as-soon-as it-was night, behold a-noise over-them, and a-shower of mist, and with that vanishing the fort, and away with them.
sentences.i: And at that, as soon as night fell, there came a noise above them, and a shower of mist, and with that the fort vanished, and was gone, and they with it.
sentences.n: Ac ar hynny 'and upon that'. gyt ac y bu nos 'as soon as it was night': bu, preterite of bot. llyma dwryf 'behold a noise': twryf softened after llyma (008 dwrwf). arnunt 'on them'. a chawat ← kawat 'shower', spirant after a; a chawat o nywl, the shower of mist of the enchantment in 008. difflannu 'vanish'. e ymdeith 'away' (ymdeith). ac wynteu 'with them': ac is a 'with'.

sentences.t: Pann welas Kicua uerch Gwyn Gloew, gwreic Pryderi, nat oed yn y llys namyn hi a Manawydan, drygyruerth a wnaeth hyt nat oed well genti y byw no'y marw.
sentences.l: When saw Cigfa daughter of-Gwyn Gloyw, wife of-Pryderi, that there-was-not in the court but she and Manawydan, lamenting she-did so-that there-was-not better with-her her living than her dying.
sentences.i: When Cigfa daughter of Gwyn Gloyw, Pryderi's wife, saw that there was no one in the court but herself and Manawydan, she lamented until she cared no more for living than for dying.
sentences.n: Pann 'when' (pan, with nn). welas ← gwelas, 3 sg. preterite, softened after pan. Kicua is Cigfa. uerch ← merch 'daughter', softened after the name. Gwyn Gloew: here spelt Gloew, in 008 Gloyw (uerch Wyn Gloyw); the same man, named Gwyn Gloyw in English. nat oed 'that there was not'. namyn 'except'. drygyruerth 'lamenting, wailing' (drwc 'bad' is its first element), with a wnaeth. hyt nat oed well genti y byw no'y marw 'so that her living was no better to her than her dying': well ← gwell, softened; genti 'with her' (gan, 3 sg. feminine); no'y 'than her' (no + 'y).

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth Manawydan, edrych ar hynny.
sentences.l: That-is what did Manawydan: looking at that.
sentences.i: Manawydan watched her.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth Manawydan, edrych 'that is what Manawydan did: looking'. ar hynny 'at that'.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb ef, “cam yd wyt arnaw, os rac uy ouyn i y drygyruerthy di. Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it, na weleisti gedymdeith gywirach noc y keffy di ui, tra uynho Duw it uot uelly.
sentences.l: “Surely,” said he, “wrong you-are on-it, if from fear of-me I that you-lament you. I it-is-that give God to surety to-you, that you-did-not-see a-companion truer than you-will-find you me, while God wills for-you to-be so.
sentences.i: “Indeed,” he said, “you are wrong in this, if it is for fear of me that you lament. I give you God as my surety, you never saw a truer companion than you will find me, so long as God wills you to be so.
sentences.n: cam yd wyt arnaw 'wrong you are on it': cam 'wrong' put first, then yd and wyt 'you are'; arnaw 'on it', ar, 3 sg. os 'if'. rac uy ouyn i 'for fear of me': rac 'because of'; ouyn is ofn 'fear', u writing /v/ (no mutation here). y drygyruerthy di 'that you lament': 2 sg. present. Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you': mach 'surety' softened after y; it 'to you'. na weleisti 'that you did not see': gweleist, 2 sg. preterite, softened after na, with ti fused. gywirach ← kywirach 'truer', softened. noc y keffy di ui 'than you will find me': keffy, 2 sg. present of caffael; ui ← mi, softened. tra uynho 'while (God) wants': mynho, present subjunctive of mynnu, softened after tra. uot ← bot, softened; uelly is yuelly 'so', here without y.

sentences.t: Y rof a Duw, bei et uwni yn dechreu uy ieuengtit, mi a gadwn gywirdeb wrth Pryderi; ac y rot titheu mi a'y cadwn. Ac na uit un ouyn arnat,” heb ef.
sentences.l: Between-me and God, if were I in beginning my youth, I it-is-that would-keep faith with Pryderi; and between-you you-for-your-part I it-is-that would-keep-it. And let-there-not-be one fear on-you,” said he.
sentences.i: Between me and God, were I in the first of my youth, I would keep faith with Pryderi; and for your sake I would keep it too. Let there be no fear upon you,” he said.
sentences.n: Y rof a Duw 'between me and God' (house): rof is rwng 'between', 1 sg. bei et uwni 'if I were': bei 'if', et the particle (yd) before the verb, and uwn i ← bwn, 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive of bot, softened, with i fused on. yn dechreu uy ieuengtit 'at the beginning of my youth'. mi a gadwn ← kadwn 'I would keep', 1 sg. imperfect with conditional sense, softened after a. gywirdeb ← kywirdeb 'faithfulness', softened as the object. y rot titheu 'between you, you for your part': rot is rwng, 2 sg., 'between you (and me)', here 'as for you, for your sake'. mi a'y cadwn 'I would keep it': 'y is the infixed object 'it', which normally softens; cadwn is written unsoftened. na uit 'let there not be': bit, 3 sg. imperative of bot, softened after na. arnat 'on you'.

sentences.t: “E rof a Duw,” heb ef, “titheu a gey y gedymdeithas a uynych y genhyf i, herwyd uyg gallu i, tra welho Duw yn bot yn y dihirwch hwnn a'r goual.”
sentences.l: “Between-me and God,” said he, “you-for-your-part it-is-that will-get the fellowship that you-may-want from-me I, according-to my ability I, while God sees-fit our being in the misery this and the care.”
sentences.i: “Between me and God,” he said, “you shall have from me what fellowship you wish, as far as I am able, so long as God sees fit for us to be in this misery and care.”
sentences.n: E rof a Duw, with e for y. titheu a gey 'you for your part shall get': key, 2 sg. present of caffael, softened after a. y gedymdeithas 'the fellowship' (house), kedymdeithas softened after the feminine article. a uynych 'that you may want': mynnych, 2 sg. present subjunctive of mynnu, softened. y genhyf i 'from me', gan, 1 sg. herwyd uyg gallu i 'according to my power': gallu after uy, with the nasal written g. tra welho Duw 'while God sees (fit)': gwelho, present subjunctive of gwelet, softened after tra. yn bot 'our being': yn is 'our'. dihirwch 'wretchedness, misery'. goual 'care, anxiety'.

sentences.t: “Duw a dalho it, a hynny a debywn i.”
sentences.l: “God may-he-repay to-you, and that it-is-that I-would-suppose.”
sentences.i: “May God repay you; that is what I would have looked for from you.”
sentences.n: Cigfa's answer, with no tag (the Red Book adds heb hi). Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you' (house; 008 has dalo): talho, present subjunctive of talu, softened after a, here spelt with h. The a after it is written small above the line in the manuscript and is brought into the line. a hynny a debywn i 'and that I would suppose': tebygwn, 1 sg. imperfect of tebygu 'suppose, expect', softened after a, written without the g (the Red Book debygwn); the scribe first wrote another n in it and marked it for deletion, and that letter is left out.

sentences.t: Ac yna kymry llywenyd ac ehouyndre o'r uorwyn o achaws hynny.
sentences.l: And then taking joy and boldness by the maiden because-of that.
sentences.i: And then the young woman took joy and heart from that.
sentences.n: kymry is a readable slip for kymryt 'taking', the verbal noun (Evans kymry, no t; the second witness kymryt); kept as written and read as kymryt. llywenyd 'joy'. ehouyndre 'fearlessness, confidence' (ehofn 'fearless'): the scribe wrote ehouyndra, marked the final a for deletion and wrote e above it, and his correction is applied (the Red Book and the second witness ehouyndra). o'r uorwyn 'by the maiden': o marks the doer of the verbal noun; morwyn softened after the feminine article. o achaws hynny 'because of that'.

sentences.t: “Ie, eneit,” heb y Manawydan, “nyt kyfle yni trigyaw yma. Yn cwn a gollyssam, ac ymborth ny allwn. Kyrchwn Loegyr; hawssaf yw in ymborth yno.”
sentences.l: “Yes, soul,” said Manawydan, “not fitting for-us to-stay here. Our dogs it-is-that we-have-lost, and feeding-ourselves we-cannot. Let-us-make-for England; easiest it-is for-us feeding-ourselves there.”
sentences.i: “Yes, friend,” said Manawydan, “it is not fit for us to stay here. We have lost our dogs, and we cannot keep ourselves. Let us make for England; it is easiest for us to make our living there.”
sentences.n: Ie 'Yes' (house). eneit 'soul', a warm address, 'friend' (as in 008). nyt kyfle yni 'it is no fit place for us': kyfle 'opportunity, fitness'; yni 'for us', y 'to', 1 pl. trigyaw 'stay, dwell'. Yn cwn a gollyssam 'our dogs we have lost': yn is 'our'; collyssam, 1 pl. preterite, softened after a. ymborth ny allwn 'feeding ourselves we cannot': the verbal noun put first, before the negative verb. After ymborth Evans prints ni allwn with every letter dotted beneath: the scribe repeated the words and then cancelled them, and they are left out. Kyrchwn Loegyr 'let us make for England': Lloegyr softened as the object. hawssaf 'easiest', superlative of hawd. in 'for us'.

sentences.t: “Yn llawen, Arglwyd,” heb hi, “a ni a wnawn hynny.”
sentences.l: “Gladly, Lord,” said she, “and we it-is-that will-do that.”
sentences.i: “Gladly, lord,” she said, “we will do so.”
sentences.n: Yn llawen 'gladly', yn with an adjective making an adverb. ni a wnawn 'we will do': gwnawn, 1 pl. present of gwneuthur, softened after a.

sentences.t: Y gyt y kerdyssant parth a Lloygyr.
sentences.l: Together it-was-that they-walked towards England.
sentences.i: They went together towards England.
sentences.n: Y gyt 'together', put first, then the particle y. kerdyssant 'they walked, went', 3 pl. preterite (kerdassant above). Lloygyr, another spelling of Lloegr, as in 008.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb hi, “pa greft a gymery di arnat? Kymer un lanweith.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said she, “what craft is-it-that you-will-take you on-you? Take one clean.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” she said, “what craft will you take up? Take a clean one.”
sentences.n: pa greft 'what craft' ← kreft, softened after pa. a gymery di 'will you take': kymery, 2 sg. present of kymryt, softened after a. arnat 'on you', to take on (as arnam in 008). Kymer 'take', 2 sg. imperative. un lanweith 'a clean one': glanweith 'clean, neat', softened after un with a feminine noun understood (kreft).

sentences.t: “Ny chymeraf i,” heb ef, “namyn crydyaeth, ual y gwneuthum gynt.”
sentences.l: “I-will-not-take I,” said he, “but shoemaking, as I-did formerly.”
sentences.i: “I will take none,” he said, “but shoemaking, as I did before.”
sentences.n: Ny chymeraf 'I will not take': kymeraf with the spirant after ny. namyn 'except, but'. crydyaeth 'shoemaking' (kryd 'shoemaker'). ual y gwneuthum 'as I did', gwneuthum, 1 sg. preterite of gwneuthur. gynt 'formerly'.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb hi, “nyt hoff honno y glanet y wr kygynhilet, kyuurd a thydi.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said she, “not pleasing that-one for so-clean for a-man so-skilful, of-equal-rank with you.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” she said, “that is no fit craft for a man as fine, as skilled and of such rank as you.”
sentences.n: nyt hoff honno 'that one (feminine, the craft) is not pleasing'. A run of equatives, closed by a thydi 'as you': glanet 'as clean, as fine' (glan); kygynhilet 'as skilful, as delicate' (ky- + kynnil 'thrifty, skilful, fine'); kyuurd 'of equal rank' (ky- + urd 'order, rank'). y glanet y wr: each y is 'to, for'; wr ← gwr, softened after y. The phrase is compressed and its exact construction is not certain, but the sense is plain. a thydi ← tydi 'you', spirant after a.

sentences.t: “Wrth honno yd af ui,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “To that-one it-is-that I-go I,” said he.
sentences.i: “That is the craft I will go to,” he said.
sentences.n: Wrth honno 'to that one': the phrase first, then the particle yd and af 'I go', 1 sg. present of mynet. ui ← mi, softened.

sentences.t: Dechreu y geluydyt a wnaeth, a chyweiraw y weith o'r cordwal teccaf a gauas yn y dref.
sentences.l: Beginning the craft he-did, and preparing his work from-the cordovan fairest that he-got in the town.
sentences.i: He began the craft, and made up his work from the finest cordovan he could get in the town.
sentences.n: Dechreu … a wnaeth 'beginning he did'. y geluydyt 'the craft' ← keluydyt, softened after the feminine article. a chyweiraw ← kyweiraw 'prepare, make up'. y weith ← gweith, softened after y 'his'. cordwal 'cordovan', as in 008; teccaf 'fairest', superlative of tec. a gauas 'that he got' ← kauas, 3 sg. preterite of caffael.

sentences.t: Ac ual y dechreussant yn lle arall, dechreu gvaegeu y'r eskidyeu o waegeu eureit, yny oed ouer a man gueith holl grydyon y dref y wrth yr eidaw ef e hun.
sentences.l: And as they-began in place other, beginning buckles to-the shoes of buckles gilded, until was idle and petty work of-all shoemakers of the town from his-own he self.
sentences.i: And as they had begun in the other place, he set about putting buckles on the shoes, gilded buckles, until the work of all the shoemakers in the town was poor and paltry beside his own.
sentences.n: ual y dechreussant 'as they began': in the last town, in 008, Manawydan had the buckles gilded. dechreu gvaegeu y'r eskidyeu 'beginning buckles for the shoes': gvaegeu 'buckles' is so written, with v (Evans gvaegeu), plural of gwaeg; then o waegeu eureit 'of gilded buckles', gwaegeu softened after o. eskidyeu 'shoes', plural of eskit. yny oed 'until was'. ouer 'vain, worthless' and man 'small, petty'. holl grydyon 'all the shoemakers' ← krydyon, softened after holl. y wrth 'compared with, beside'. yr eidaw ef e hun 'his own self's': eidaw 'his' as a pronoun, 'his own', strengthened by ef e hun 'he himself'.

sentences.t: A thra geffit y gantaw nac eskit na hossan, ni phrynit y gan ereill dim.
sentences.l: And while was-got from-him either shoe or hose, there-was-not-bought from others anything.
sentences.i: And so long as shoe or hose could be had from him, nothing was bought from anyone else.
sentences.n: The pattern of 008: tra geffit 'while (any) was got', keffit, impersonal imperfect of caffael, softened after tra; ni phrynit 'there was not bought', prynit, impersonal imperfect of prynu, with the spirant after ni. y gantaw 'from him'. nac … na 'either … or'. y gan ereill 'from others'.

sentences.t: A blwyn yuelly a dreulwys yno, ynyd oed y crydyon yn dala kynuigen a chynghoruyn wrthaw.
sentences.l: And a-year thus he-spent there, until were the shoemakers holding envy and jealousy against-him.
sentences.i: And he spent a year there so, until the shoemakers were nursing envy and jealousy against him.
sentences.n: blwyn is a slip for blwydyn 'year' (Evans Ablwyn, plain on the image; the Red Book blwydyn): kept as written and read as blwydyn. a dreulwys 'he spent': treulwys, 3 sg. preterite in -wys, softened after a; the object put first. ynyd oed 'until were': yny 'until' joined to the particle yd before oed. dala 'hold, keep'. kynuigen 'envy' a chynghoruyn ← kynghoruyn 'envy, jealousy'. wrthaw 'towards him, against him', wrth, 3 sg.

sentences.t: Ac yny doeth rybudyeu idaw, a menegi uot y crydyon wedy duunaw ar y lad.
sentences.l: And until came warnings to-him, and telling that were the shoemakers after agreeing on his killing.
sentences.i: And at length warnings came to him, and he was told that the shoemakers had agreed to kill him.
sentences.n: yny doeth 'until came': the sentence takes up the last one, 'until in the end'. rybudyeu 'warnings', plural of rybud. idaw 'to him'. a menegi 'and telling', the verbal noun with no stated subject: 'and it was told'. uot ← bot, softened. wedy duunaw ar 'after agreeing on': duunaw 'agree, become one' (du- + un). y lad ← llad 'killing', softened after y 'his': 'to kill him'.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Kicua, “pam y diodeuir hynn gan y tayogeu?”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Cigfa, “why is-borne this from the churls?”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Cigfa, “why should this be borne from these churls?”
sentences.n: pam 'why'. y diodeuir 'is suffered': the impersonal present in -ir of diodef (diodeu-) 'suffer, endure'. tayogeu 'churls', plural of tayawc (as in 008).

sentences.t: “Nac ef,” heb ynteu, “ni a aem eissoes y Dyuet.”
sentences.l: “Not it,” said he-for-his-part, “we it-is-that would-go nevertheless to Dyfed.”
sentences.i: “No,” he said; “we had better go to Dyfed after all.”
sentences.n: Nac ef 'not it' = No (as in 008). ni a aem 'we would go': aem, 1 pl. imperfect of mynet, with the conditional sense of the imperfect, 'we should go, we had better go'. eissoes 'nevertheless, after all'.

sentences.t: Dyuet a gyrchyssant.
sentences.l: Dyfed it-was-that they-made-for.
sentences.i: They made for Dyfed.
sentences.n: The abnormal sentence with the object first: Dyuet a gyrchyssant, as Arberth a gyrchyssant at the opening of the part.

sentences.t: Sef a oruc Manawydan, pan gychwynnwys parth a Dyuet, dwyn beich o wenith gantaw, a chyrchu Arberth, a chyuanhedu yno.
sentences.l: That-is what did Manawydan, when he-set-out towards Dyfed: carrying a-load of wheat with-him, and making-for Arberth, and settling there.
sentences.i: When he set out for Dyfed, Manawydan took a load of wheat with him; and he made for Arberth, and settled there.
sentences.n: Sef a oruc Manawydan … dwyn 'that is what Manawydan did: carrying'. pan gychwynnwys 'when he set out': kychwynnwys, 3 sg. preterite in -wys, softened after pan. beich 'load, burden'. o wenith ← gwenith 'wheat', softened after o. a chyuanhedu ← kyuanhedu 'dwell, settle'.

sentences.t: Ac nit oed dim digriuach gantaw no gwelet Arberth a'r tirogaeth y buassei yn hela, ef a Pryderi a Riannon gyt ac wynt.
sentences.l: And there-was-not anything more-pleasing with-him than seeing Arberth and the lands that he-had-been hunting, he and Pryderi and Rhiannon with them.
sentences.i: And nothing pleased him more than to see Arberth and the lands where he used to hunt, he and Pryderi, and Rhiannon with them.
sentences.n: nit oed dim 'there was not anything'. digriuach 'more pleasant', comparative of digrif. gantaw 'with him', to him. no 'than'. tirogaeth 'lands, territory' (tir 'land'). y buassei yn hela 'where he had been hunting': buassei, 3 sg. pluperfect of bot. ef a Pryderi: Pryderi is left unmutated after a 'and', as names often are.

sentences.t: Dechreu a wnaeth kyneuinaw a hela pyscawt a llydnot ar eu gual yno.
sentences.l: Beginning he-did accustoming-himself with hunting fish and wild-beasts on their lair there.
sentences.i: There he began to grow used to taking fish, and wild beasts in their lairs.
sentences.n: Dechreu a wnaeth kyneuinaw 'beginning he did, growing accustomed': kyneuinaw 'become accustomed, settle in'. a hela may be 'with hunting' (kyneuinaw a 'get used to') or 'and hunting'; either reading gives good sense. hela pyscawt 'hunting fish', fishing. llydnot 'young beasts, wild animals', plural of llwdn. ar eu gual 'in their lair': gwal 'lair', spelt gu-.

sentences.t: Ac yn ol hynny dechreu ryuoryaw.
sentences.l: And after that, beginning tilling.
sentences.i: And after that he began to till the ground.
sentences.n: yn ol hynny 'after that'. ryuoryaw is a rare verb; from the context it means to break and work the ground, to till, but the exact sense is uncertain; the initial r writes rh.

sentences.t: Ac yn ol hynny, heu groft, a'r eil, a'r trydyd.
sentences.l: And after that, sowing a-croft, and the second, and the third.
sentences.i: And after that he sowed a croft, and a second, and a third.
sentences.n: heu 'sow' (hau). groft ← kroft 'croft, small field', softened; here written with t, elsewhere in the part grofd. a'r eil 'and the second'. a'r trydyd 'and the third', the masculine form, where the tryded grofd of paragraph 14 treats the croft as feminine.

sentences.t: Ac nachaf y guenith yn kyuot yn oreu yn y byt, a'e deir grofd yn llwydaw yn un dwf, hyt na welsei dyn wenith tegach noc ef.
sentences.l: And behold the wheat rising best in the world, and his three crofts prospering in one growth, so-that had-not-seen a-man wheat fairer than it.
sentences.i: And behold, the wheat came up the best in the world, and his three crofts throve as one growth, so that no man had seen finer wheat than it.
sentences.n: nachaf 'behold', a synonym of llyma (and like it softens what follows). kyuot 'rise', a form of kyuodi. yn oreu yn y byt 'best in the world': goreu softened after yn. a'e deir grofd 'and his three crofts': teir, the feminine of tri, softened after 'e 'his', and kroft softened after teir. llwydaw 'prosper' (as in 008). yn un dwf 'in one growth': twf softened after un, the crops alike. na welsei dyn 'no man had seen': gwelsei, 3 sg. pluperfect, softened after na. wenith ← gwenith, softened as the object. tegach 'fairer', comparative of tec.

sentences.t: Treulaw amseroed y ulwydyn a wnaeth.
sentences.l: Spending the seasons of the year he-did.
sentences.i: He passed the seasons of the year.
sentences.n: Treulaw … a wnaeth 'spending he did'. amseroed 'times, seasons', plural of amser. y ulwydyn 'the year': blwydyn softened after the feminine article.

sentences.t: Nachaf y kynhaeaf yn dyuot; ac y edrych un o'e rofdeu y doeth.
sentences.l: Behold the harvest coming; and to look-at one of his crofts it-was-that he-came.
sentences.i: And behold, the harvest was coming on; and he came to look at one of his crofts.
sentences.n: Nachaf … yn dyuot 'behold … coming'. kynhaeaf 'harvest, autumn'. y edrych 'to look at'. o'e rofdeu 'of his crofts': krofdeu, plural, after 'e 'his', is written with no initial at all, as if the g of grofd were the root and dropped in the soft mutation, as the g of a word like gwenith would; the spelling is odd but the word is clear. y doeth 'he came', after the fronted phrase.

sentences.t: Nachaf honno yn aeduet.
sentences.l: Behold that-one ripe.
sentences.i: And behold, that one was ripe.
sentences.n: honno 'that one' (feminine, the croft). yn aeduet 'ripe', predicative yn, with no verb.

sentences.t: “Mi a uynhaf uedi honn auory,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I it-is-that will-want reaping this-one tomorrow,” said he.
sentences.i: “I will reap this one tomorrow,” he said.
sentences.n: mi a uynhaf 'I will want, I mean to': mynhaf, 1 sg. present of mynnu, softened after a. uedi ← medi 'reap', softened after the verb. honn 'this one' (feminine). auory 'tomorrow'.

sentences.t: Dyuot tra y gefyn y nos honno hyt yn Arberth.
sentences.l: Coming beyond his back that night as-far-as Arberth.
sentences.i: That night he went back to Arberth.
sentences.n: Dyuot 'coming', the verbal noun alone. tra y gefyn 'beyond his back' = back again: tra 'beyond' and kefyn 'back', softened after y 'his'. y nos honno 'that night'. hyt yn 'as far as, right to'.

sentences.t: E bore glas dranoeth, dyuot y uynnu medi y grofd.
sentences.l: The morning grey next-day, coming to want reaping the croft.
sentences.i: In the grey of the morning, the next day, he came intending to reap the croft.
sentences.n: E bore glas 'the grey morning', at dawn: e is the article y. dranoeth ← trannoeth 'next day', softened as an adverb of time. y uynnu ← mynnu, softened after y 'to': 'to want, intending'. medi 'reap', here unsoftened after the verbal noun. y grofd 'the croft': kroft softened after the feminine article.

sentences.t: Pan daw, nyt oed namyn y calaf yn llwm, wedy daruot torri pob un yn y doi yn y dywyssen o'r keleuyn, a mynet e ymdeith a'r tewys yn hollawl, ac adaw y calaf yno yn llwm.
sentences.l: When he-comes, there-was-not but the stalks bare, after breaking every one where it-would-come in the ear from-the stalk, and going away with-the ears entirely, and leaving the stalks there bare.
sentences.i: When he came, there was nothing but the bare straw: every stalk had been broken off where the ear grew from it, and the ears all carried away, and the straw left there bare.
sentences.n: Pan daw 'when he comes'. calaf 'stalks, straw', a collective. yn llwm 'bare'. wedy daruot torri 'after breaking had been done': daruot 'come about, be finished' with a verbal noun makes a pluperfect, 'had been broken'. The words yn y doi yn y dywyssen o'r keleuyn are hard; they are so written in the White Book (and the Red Book has the same), and the second witness drops the second yn. doi is perhaps the imperfect of dyuot 'come'; the clause is taken to mean 'where the ear came out of the stalk', but the sense is uncertain. tywyssen 'ear of corn', softened after the article; keleuyn 'stalk', the single of calaf. e ymdeith 'away'. a'r tewys 'with the ears': tewys, plural of tywyssen (spelt tywys later). yn hollawl 'entirely'.

sentences.t: Ryuedu hynny yn uawr a wnaeth, a dyuot y edrych grofd arall; nachaf honno yn aeduet.
sentences.l: Marvelling at-that greatly he-did, and coming to look-at a-croft other; behold that-one ripe.
sentences.i: He marvelled greatly at that, and went to look at another croft; and behold, that one was ripe.
sentences.n: Ryuedu … a wnaeth 'marvelling he did'. yn uawr 'greatly' ← mawr, softened after yn. grofd arall 'another croft', kroft softened as the object. nachaf honno yn aeduet, as before.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb ef, “mi a uynhaf medi honn auory.”
sentences.l: “Surely,” said he, “I it-is-that will-want reaping this-one tomorrow.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” he said, “I will reap this one tomorrow.”
sentences.n: His words of the first croft, but now medi is unsoftened after uynhaf (above uedi).

sentences.t: A thrannoeth dyuot ar uedwl medi honno.
sentences.l: And next-day coming on intention reaping that-one.
sentences.i: And the next day he came, meaning to reap it.
sentences.n: A thrannoeth ← trannoeth, spirant after a. ar uedwl 'on the thought of', intending: medwl softened after ar. honno 'that one'.

sentences.t: A phan daw, nit oed dim namyn y calaf llwm.
sentences.l: And when he-comes, there-was-not anything but the stalks bare.
sentences.i: And when he came, there was nothing but the bare straw.
sentences.n: A phan ← pan, spirant after a. nit oed dim namyn 'there was nothing but'. y calaf llwm 'the bare straw', the adjective here after its noun with no yn.

sentences.t: “Oy a Arglwyd Duw,” heb ef, “pwy yssyd yn gorfen uyn diua i? A mi a'e gwnn: y neb a dechreuis uyn diua yssyd yn y orffen, ac a diuawys y wlad gyt a mi.”
sentences.l: “Oh Lord God,” said he, “who is finishing my destroying I? And I it-is-that know-it: the one who began my destroying is finishing it, and who destroyed the land along with me.”
sentences.i: “Oh Lord God,” he said, “who is it that is finishing my ruin? And I know it: whoever began my ruin is finishing it, he who laid waste the land along with me.”
sentences.n: Oy a Arglwyd Duw 'Oh Lord God', as in 008. pwy yssyd 'who is (it that)'. gorfen 'finish' (gorffen, here with a single f; below orffen). uyn diua i 'my destruction': uy 'my' with the nasal written n before d (= fy nifa). A mi a'e gwnn 'and I know it': 'e the infixed object, gwnn 'I know', 1 sg. present of gwybot. y neb a dechreuis 'the one who began': dechreuis, 3 sg. preterite in -is. yn y orffen 'finishing it': y 'its' before the verbal noun, gorffen softened. a diuawys 'who destroyed': diuawys, 3 sg. preterite in -wys of diua. y wlad 'the land', with d for the t of gwlat elsewhere. gyt a mi 'together with me': the land laid waste and his crops with it.

sentences.t: Dyuot y edrych y tryded grofd.
sentences.l: Coming to look-at the third croft.
sentences.i: He came to look at the third croft.
sentences.n: y tryded grofd 'the third croft': tryded is the feminine ordinal, and kroft is softened after it.

sentences.t: Pan doeth, ny welsei dyn wenith degach, a hwnnw yn aeduet.
sentences.l: When he-came, had-not-seen a-man wheat fairer, and that ripe.
sentences.i: When he came, no man had ever seen finer wheat, and it was ripe.
sentences.n: ny welsei dyn 'no man had seen', as in the account of the sowing. degach ← tegach 'fairer', softened after the noun. a hwnnw yn aeduet 'and that (the wheat, masculine) ripe'.

sentences.t: “Meuyl y mi,” heb ef, “ony wylaf i heno. A duc yr yt arall a daw y dwyn hwnn, a mi a wybydaf beth yw.”
sentences.l: “Shame to me,” said he, “if-not I-watch I tonight. The-one-who took the corn other will-come to take this, and I it-is-that will-know what it-is.”
sentences.i: “Shame on me,” he said, “if I do not keep watch tonight. Whoever carried off the other corn will come to carry off this, and I shall know what it is.”
sentences.n: Meuyl y mi 'shame to me' (house: 'shame on me'). ony 'if not'. wylaf ← gwylaf 'I watch', 1 sg. present of gwylat, softened after ony. A duc 'that which took, the one who took': a, the relative used without an antecedent; duc, 3 sg. preterite of dwyn 'carry off'. yr yt arall 'the other corn' (yt 'corn, grain'). a daw 'will come': daw, 3 sg. present of dyuot. y dwyn hwnn 'to take this'. mi a wybydaf 'I will know': gwybydaf, future of gwybot, softened after a.

sentences.t: A chymryt y arueu a wnaeth, a dechreu gwylat y grofd.
sentences.l: And taking his arms he-did, and beginning watching the croft.
sentences.i: He took up his arms, and began to watch the croft.
sentences.n: A chymryt ← kymryt, spirant after a. y arueu 'his arms', plural of arf. gwylat 'watch, keep vigil'.

sentences.t: A menegi a wnaeth y Kicua hynny oll.
sentences.l: And telling he-did to Cigfa that all.
sentences.i: And he told Cigfa all of it.
sentences.n: A menegi a wnaeth 'and telling he did'. y Kicua 'to Cigfa': the name is not softened after y 'to'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hi, “beth yssyd y'th uryt ti?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she, “what is in-your mind you?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “and what is in your mind?”
sentences.n: Ie 'Yes' (house). beth yssyd 'what is'. y'th uryt 'in your mind': y is yn 'in' before 'th 'your', which softens bryt. ti repeats 'your'.

sentences.t: “Mi a wylaf y grofd heno,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I it-is-that will-watch the croft tonight,” said he.
sentences.i: “I will watch the croft tonight,” he said.
sentences.n: mi a wylaf 'I will watch', as above.

sentences.t: E wylat y groft yd aeth.
sentences.l: To watch the croft it-was-that he-went.
sentences.i: He went to watch the croft.
sentences.n: E wylat 'to watch': e is y 'to', which softens gwylat. y groft: so written, with t (certain on the image), where the part elsewhere has grofd. yd aeth 'he went', aeth 3 sg. preterite of mynet, after the fronted phrase.

sentences.t: Ac ual y byd am hanner nos yuelly, nachaf twryf mwyhaf yn y byt; sef a wnaeth ynteu, edrych.
sentences.l: And as he-is about half night thus, behold a-noise greatest in the world; that-is what did he-for-his-part: looking.
sentences.i: And as he was so, about midnight, there came the loudest noise in the world; and he looked.
sentences.n: ual y byd 'as he is': the vivid present of bot, as in the First Branch. am hanner nos 'about midnight'. nachaf twryf 'behold a noise': here twryf stands unsoftened after nachaf. mwyhaf 'greatest', superlative of mawr. sef a wnaeth ynteu, edrych 'that is what he did: looking'.

sentences.t: Llyma eliwlu y byd o lygot, a chyfrif na messur ny ellit ar hynny.
sentences.l: Behold a-host the world's of mice, and counting nor measure there-could-not-be on that.
sentences.i: Behold, the greatest host of mice in the world, and there was no counting or measuring it.
sentences.n: Llyma 'behold'. eliwlu is a rare word; it seems to mean 'a host, a vast number', and y byd 'of the world' makes it the greatest in the world; the meaning is from the context and is not certain. o lygot 'of mice' ← llygot, softened after o. a chyfrif ← kyfrif 'counting', spirant after a. na messur 'nor measure'. ny ellit 'there could not be': gellit, impersonal imperfect of gallu, softened after ny. ar hynny 'on that'.

sentences.t: Ac ny wydat yny uyd y llygot yn guan adan y grofd, a phob un yn drigyaw ar hyt y kyleuyn, ac yn y estwng genti, ac yn torri y dywyssen, ac yn guan a'r tywys e ymdeith, ac yn adaw y calaf yno.
sentences.l: And he-did-not-know until are the mice rushing into the croft, and every one climbing along the stalk, and its lowering with-her, and breaking the ear, and rushing with-the ears away, and leaving the stalks there.
sentences.i: And before he knew it the mice were pouring into the croft, each of them climbing up the stalk and bending it down with her weight, and breaking off the ear, and rushing away with the ears, and leaving the straw there.
sentences.n: ny wydat 'he did not know': gwydat, imperfect of gwybot, softened after ny. yny uyd 'until are': byd, the vivid present of bot, softened after yny: 'before he knew, the mice were …'. yn guan 'rushing, thrusting'. adan 'under, into'. drigyaw is dringaw 'climb', written without n. ar hyt y kyleuyn 'along the stalk' (keleuyn, spelt with y). yn y estwng 'its lowering' = bending it down: y 'its' before the verbal noun. genti 'with her': gan, 3 sg. feminine, for the mouse (llygoden is feminine). torri y dywyssen 'breaking the ear': tywyssen softened after the article. e ymdeith 'away'.

sentences.t: Ac ni wydyat ef uot un keleuyn yno ny bei lygoden am pob un.
sentences.l: And he-did-not-know he there-to-be one stalk there that there-was-not a-mouse about every one.
sentences.i: And he could not make out a single stalk there without a mouse on it.
sentences.n: ni wydyat ef 'he did not know': the same verb as before, spelt wydyat. uot ← bot 'to be', softened after the verb. ny bei 'there was not': bei, imperfect subjunctive of bot, in a negative relative clause. lygoden ← llygoden 'mouse', softened after bei. am pob un 'about every one', repeating the idea of keleuyn.

sentences.t: Ac a gymerynt eu hynt racdunt a'r tywys gantunt.
sentences.l: And it-was-that they-would-take their way before-them and the ears with-them.
sentences.i: And off they went on their way, with the ears in their keeping.
sentences.n: Ac a gymerynt: the sentence opens with the particle a and the verb, the subject (the mice) understood from before. kymerynt, 3 pl. imperfect of kymryt, softened after a. eu hynt 'their way, their course'. racdunt 'before them', onwards (rac, 3 pl.). a'r tywys gantunt 'and the ears with them': gantunt 'with them' (gan, 3 pl.).

sentences.t: Ac yna, rwng dicter a llit, taraw ym plith y llygot a wnaeth.
sentences.l: And then, between anger and wrath, striking among the mice he-did.
sentences.i: And then, between anger and wrath, he struck in among the mice.
sentences.n: rwng 'between'. dicter 'anger'. llit 'wrath'. taraw … a wnaeth 'striking he did'. ym plith 'among': yn before p becomes ym, the nasal mutation of plith not written.

sentences.t: A mwy noc ar y gwydbet neu yr adar yn yr awyr, ni chytdremei ef ar yr un ohonunt wy, eithyr un a welei yn amdrom, ual y tebygei na allei un pedestric.
sentences.l: And more than on the gnats or the birds in the air, he-could-not-keep-in-sight he on the one of-them them, except one he-saw heavy, as he-would-suppose that she-could-not one going-on-foot.
sentences.i: And he could no more keep his eye on any one of them than on midges or the birds in the air, except for one that he saw was heavy, so heavy he judged she could not go at any pace.
sentences.n: mwy noc ar … ni … 'more than on … not', no more than on. gwydbet 'midges, gnats' (gwybed, here written with d). ni chytdremei 'he could not keep in sight': kytdremu 'look together, keep sight of' (kyt- + drem 'look'), imperfect, with the spirant after ni; so Evans, where the second witness has ny. ohonunt wy 'of them', the pronoun doubled. eithyr 'except'. amdrom 'very heavy' (am- + trwm); one may suppose with young. ual y tebygei 'so that he thought': tebygei, imperfect of tebygu. na allei 'that she could not': gallei softened after na. un pedestric 'one (bit of) going on foot': pedestric 'going on foot, speed of foot', from Latin pedester; the phrase means she could not run, but its construction is not certain.

sentences.t: Yn ol honno y kerdwys ef, a'y dala a wnaeth, a'y dodi a wnaeth yn y uanec, ac a llinin rwymaw geneu y uanec, a'y chadw gantaw, a chyrchu y llys.
sentences.l: After that-one it-was-that he-walked, and her catching he-did, and her putting he-did in his glove, and with a-string tying the mouth of the glove, and her keeping with-him, and making-for the court.
sentences.i: He went after that one, and caught her, and put her in his glove, and tied up the mouth of the glove with a string, and kept her by him, and made for the court.
sentences.n: Yn ol honno 'after that one' (feminine, the mouse), put first, then the particle y. kerdwys 'walked, went', 3 sg. preterite in -wys of kerdet. a'y dala 'and her catching': 'y 'her' before the verbal noun marks its object. a'y dodi 'and her putting'. y uanec ← manec 'glove', softened after y 'his'. ac a llinin 'and with a string': a 'with'; llinin 'thread, string'. rwymaw ← rhwymaw 'tie', softened after the phrase put before it (or simply r writing rh). geneu 'mouth', the opening of the glove. a'y chadw 'and her keeping': kadw with the spirant after 'y 'her'. a chyrchu y llys 'and making for the court'.
